newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - CBOE filed to list Dow indices - CBOE head.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - CBOE filed to list Dow indices - CBOE head.

text.p: The Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) has filed a proposal with Dow Jones & Co to list options on the company's popular Dow Jones stock averages, CBOE chairman William Brodsky said.
Brodsky said the exchange filed its proposal on April 25.

"I know that they're trying to review all the proposals -- they have many -- and get back to people in a reasonable time," he said in an interview at an options industry conference. "It's not protracted."

Dow Jones owns one of the most widely watched U.S. market measures, the Dow Jones industrial average .DJI as well as the Dow Jones transportation average .DJT and the Dow Jones utility average .DJU and a family of foriegn stck market indices.
Brodsky said the CBOE's plan to halve the S&P 100 stock index .OEX has been put on the back burner, but the exchange continues to check with member firms for their views on such a split.
"My feeling is the pressure seems to have subsided a bit to do it," he said. "There was a call to do it and I think there were some valid reasons to do it.
"Whenever you're dealing with the biggest product that the institution has, the one thing you don't do is rush into it," he said.

He said the exchange's proposal to list options on a mutual fund index is pending approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission and that it will be listing its sixth structured product -- a Bear Stearns S&P-linked note due May 2003 -- next week.
"That's starting to become a nice little niche business of ours," he said, referring to the CBOE's listing of structured products. "We have made a real commitment in that area."
